questions.stem: In paediatric anaesthesia, why is inhalational induction a common choice?
What key benefit does inhalational induction offer in a difficult airway?
What advantage of inhalational induction relates to the depth of anaesthesia?
questions.answer: Depth can be changed gradually, with cardiovascular stability.

questions.stem: Which bronchial effect do volatile agents and propofol share?
Why may children find inhalational induction distressing?
questions.answer: They may fear the mask; the unfamiliar smell causes anxiety.

questions.stem: Compared with IV induction, what is a disadvantage of inhalational induction?
questions.answer: Slower and possibly less smooth induction.

questions.stem: Compared with propofol, which airway problems are more likely with inhalational induction?
questions.answer: More laryngospasm, bronchospasm, severe coughing and desaturation.

questions.stem: In which patients should inhalational induction not be used?
questions.answer: Rapid sequence induction or full stomach.

questions.stem: What is the main airway risk of inhalational induction in obstructive sleep apnoea?
Why is sevoflurane the usual agent for inhalational induction?
options: Strongly pungent with high blood:gas solubility
Not pungent, low blood:gas solubility, smooth induction
Rapid onset but high blood:gas solubility

questions.stem: In tidal volume inhalational induction, how is the agent delivered?
questions.answer: Normal breathing through a face mask.

questions.stem: In vital capacity inhalational induction, what does the patient do first?
In inhalational induction, what high delivered sevoflurane concentration is used?
What effect does adding nitrous oxide have on inhalational induction?
For which airway procedures is inhalational induction suitable?
Intubating on sevoflurane alone needs what depth of anaesthesia?
Why is hypotension more likely when intubating on sevoflurane alone?
questions.answer: Deep anaesthesia is needed, typically MAC 2.0.

questions.stem: What is co-induction in inhalational or IV induction?
questions.answer: Combining drugs for a greater effect than each alone.

questions.stem: When is co-induction useful?
questions.answer: When haemodynamically unstable or when spontaneous ventilation is wanted.

questions.stem: What is an example co-induction regimen using sevoflurane and propofol?
Historically, what role did inhalational induction have in difficult airway management?
In a difficult airway, what oxygenation advantage does inhalational induction offer?
questions.answer: Spontaneous ventilation, and so oxygenation, is more likely kept.

questions.stem: In a difficult airway, what makes inhalational induction slow to reach depth?
questions.answer: Longer stage 2 and laryngospasm; obstruction makes it slower still.

In NAP4, in how many of 16 inhalational inductions was spontaneous ventilation lost?
